blocks.task_summary: For f(x) = cos(x - k) with k = π/2 and domain 0 ≤ x ≤ a, find the largest a for which f⁻¹ exists.
method_path: Transform f(x) = cos(x - π/2) to sin(x)
Identify that sin(x) is strictly increasing on [0, π/2] and therefore one-to-one
Conclude a = π/2 is the largest value preserving one-to-one property
accepted_alternatives: Graphical approach via sketching f(x) = sin(x) and applying the horizontal line test.

evidence.basis: a = π/2, A2. Note: For sinusoidal graph through the origin seen with incorrect a, or use of horizontal line test with incorrect a, award A1A0.

blocks.task_summary: For f(x) = cos(x - k) with k = π, find the largest a for which f⁻¹ exists.
method_path: Recognize that -cos(x) is strictly increasing on [0, π]

blocks.task_summary: For f(x) = cos(x - k) with π < k < 2π, find the largest a for which f⁻¹ exists, giving answer in terms of k.
method_path: Compute f'(x) = -sin(x - k) and evaluate sign at x = 0: f'(0) = sin(k) < 0 for k ∈ (π, 2π)
Find first positive x where f'(x) = 0 by solving sin(x - k) = 0, giving x = k - π
Conclude that f is strictly decreasing and one-to-one on [0, k - π], so a = k - π
accepted_alternatives: Sketch the sinusoidal curve shifted right by k, observe it crosses the y-axis decreasing, and the first turning point occurs at x = k - π.

evidence.basis: sketch showing sinusoidal shape decreasing as it crosses the y-axis (below or above the origin) (A1). a = k - π, A1.
